Hence equilibrium constant for ionization <math><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>⇌</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></math> is.The value of ‘x’ is.

solution.text:
NH4OHaq+H+aq⇌NH4+aq+H2Ol

K1=N+H4NH4OHH+=1.8×109

NH4OHaq⇌NH4+aq+OH-aq

K2=NH4+OH-NH4OH

Multiply this by H+ and divide also 

K2=NH4+OH-H+NH4OH H+=K1×Kw

=1.8×109×1.0×10-14=18×10-6

value of x = 18.
